data.name: Chintan
data.gender_notes: Chintan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Chintan is a Sanskrit word derived from the root 'chin' meaning 'to think'. This name signifies one who is engaged in deep thought, reflection or meditation. The name Chintan carries the meaning “Thought, Reflection” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chintan usually hope their child will grow to embody thought, reflection and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Chintan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Thought, Reflection.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chintan total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Chintan holds a significant cultural value in Hindu traditions, representing intellectual, contemplative, and introspective individuals. It is believed that such individuals make invaluable contributions to society, driving progress and innovation through their deep thought processes.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Chintan is an embodiment of the practice of Dhyana Yoga or meditation, which aims to connect an individual with their higher self and attain blissful consciousness. Engaging in deep thought and reflection is a way to seek self-realization, promote inner peace and gain wisdom. Thus, Chintan is a name that carries profound spiritual significance.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Chintan signifies the seat of consciousness and thought in Hinduism. It is the innermost space of the mind where one can contemplate, reflect and meditate. The name encourages one to be introspective and focus on the inner self for spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Chintan is a name mentioned in the Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic. The name Chintan carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
